newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on ING U.S. takeover.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on ING U.S. takeover.

text.p: Dutch banking and insurance group ING Groep NV said on Tuesday it was buying Equitable of Iowa Companies for $68 per share with its own shares and/or cash in a deal worth $2.2 billion.
Below is a selection of analysts' comments.
HEINIE HAKKER, BARCLAYS DE ZOETE WEDD:

"An acquisition in the field of life insurance in the U.S. was expected as they have said before they were on the lookout for it. The move is meaningful as it doubles ING's life insurance premium income, but compared to the group's size, the takeover is not that big. It probably will not stop ING coming with another (takeover) as they've said before that they want to expand in banking in Europe and in the investment business. The price they are willing to pay for Iowa is reasonable at about 15 times the group's profit. The main thing is that they (ING) needed more scale."

"With this deal, ING realises one of its two main targets, namely expanding its U.S. life insurance business. It's a good strategic move, notably because it will increase the stability of ING's earnings since the proportion of life insurance gets bigger. They're paying quite a heavy price, but that's no more than normal given there are many parties interested in the U.S. insurance market. We had already included a major acquisition in our EPS estimates, so these will probably remain the same at 5.10 guilders for this year and 5.65 for 1998. We have a share price target of 120 guilders for the end of 1998."

"This is a very good takeover and the're paying a nice price. With this move ING is shifting toward higher growth markets. They're going from traditional life insurance, growing between zero and two percent a year, toward annuity insurance which grows ten to 15 percent a year, a good addition to the current activities. There will be synergies, the bigger size will strengthen market position. The share price reaction is late but is justified. I expected a bigger acquisition, there will certainly be add-on acquisitions. I will raise my EPS forecasts for 1998 by at least 0.10 guilders on this buy."

"It is positive that it took them a while to make this move as a U.S. takeover had been expected. Iowa looks a healthy company and ING needed more scale. They probably will announce another (big) acquisition in the U.S. in three to four years. The deal looks positive and, as ING says, it will probably have a slightly positive impact on earnings per share. You can argue that the price is high. ING is paying 17 times next year's profit for Iowa. But ING is able to afford it as they are expensive themselves. (ING's current price/earnings ratio is almost 21).
